7zip_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. 7-Zip keeps its settings and history in the registry (HKCU\Software\7-Zip); an %APPDATA%\7-Zip folder is not a standard 7-Zip cache.
7zip_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
7zip_cache.risk: Whatever another tool or a portable setup put there (settings, language files) would be lost; no cache benefit.
7zip_cache.catalog_concern: Path is a whole app folder, not a cache. Label (history/extraction output) does not match 7-Zip's real behaviour; extraction temp goes to %TEMP%.

acronis_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor for this exact path. Acronis True Image writes operation logs; this targets only a Logs subfolder of the user's Acronis data.
acronis_cache.used_for: Logs are read only when troubleshooting or by Acronis support. Deleting them does not affect backups; new logs are written on the next operation.
acronis_cache.risk: Lost diagnostics: you cannot show support what happened on a failed backup. Backup archives and catalogs are not in this folder.
acronis_cache.before_cleaning: Close Acronis and make sure no backup is running.
acronis_cache.catalog_concern: Label says 'backup catalog' but the path is Logs only, which is the right, narrow choice. Acronis' main logs live under ProgramData, so this may find little.

aida64_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. AIDA64 normally keeps its settings and license next to its program files; %APPDATA%\AIDA64 is not a documented cache.
aida64_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
aida64_cache.risk: Possible loss of settings, sensor-panel layouts or saved reports.
aida64_cache.catalog_concern: Whole app folder, not a cache.

aomei_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. A whole AOMEI data folder can hold backup task definitions and history that Backupper needs to find and restore its images.
aomei_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
aomei_cache.risk: Backup tasks and their history could disappear from the app, making scheduled backups stop or restores harder.
aomei_cache.catalog_concern: Whole app folder holding backup task configuration; correctly disabled.

auslogics_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Auslogics tools keep 'Rescue Center' backups (registry and file backups made before changes) under their data folder.
auslogics_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
auslogics_cache.risk: Loses the ability to undo changes Auslogics made to the registry or system.
auslogics_cache.catalog_concern: Registry backups are undo data, not cache; correctly disabled.

bandizip_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. A whole Bandizip settings folder, not a known cache.
bandizip_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
bandizip_cache.catalog_concern: Whole app folder, not a cache.

bitwarden_desktop_cache.what: The Chromium (Electron) HTTP cache of the Bitwarden desktop app. The encrypted vault itself is data.json in %APPDATA%\Bitwarden, a sibling of this folder, and is not targeted.
bitwarden_desktop_cache.used_for: Speeds up loading the app's web resources. Rebuilt automatically the next time Bitwarden runs.
bitwarden_desktop_cache.risk: None known for the cache folder. Never widen the path to the parent folder: that holds data.json (offline vault, login state).
bitwarden_desktop_cache.catalog_concern: Only 'cache' is targeted, good. The Microsoft Store build lives under Packages\8bitSolutionsLLC.bitwardendesktop_*\LocalCache\Roaming\Bitwarden and is not covered. Label mentions logs, which are not targeted.

bleachbit_cache.what: BleachBit's own data folder: its settings file (bleachbit.ini) and downloaded/custom cleaner definitions (CleanerML).
bleachbit_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
bleachbit_cache.risk: Loses BleachBit settings, whitelists and custom cleaners.
bleachbit_cache.catalog_concern: Whole app folder, not a cache.

bluetooth_cache.what: Not documented by Microsoft. Bluetooth pairings are stored in the registry (BTHPORT\Parameters\Keys), and %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\INF is not a documented Bluetooth location.
bluetooth_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
bluetooth_cache.risk: Unknown contents under a Windows folder; no documented cache benefit. Label suggests pairing records, which would mean re-pairing devices.
bluetooth_cache.catalog_concern: Paths and label are not backed by any Microsoft documentation; keep disabled.

ccleaner_cache.what: CCleaner's own data/settings folder (settings, custom include/exclude rules), not a documented cache.
ccleaner_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
ccleaner_cache.risk: Loses CCleaner settings and custom cleaning rules.
ccleaner_cache.catalog_concern: Whole app folder, not a cache.

clevo_ControlCenter_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. A whole Clevo Control Center data folder, which may include fan profiles.
clevo_ControlCenter_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
clevo_ControlCenter_cache.risk: Possible loss of custom fan/power profiles.
clevo_ControlCenter_cache.catalog_concern: Whole app folder, not a cache.

clipboard.what: Not documented by Microsoft. Temporary 'pending'/'inProgress' .tmp files in the Windows clipboard history folder, apparently left over from items being written to clipboard history.
clipboard.used_for: Windows creates such temporary files while saving clipboard history items. Leftovers are not used again.
clipboard.risk: A file matching the pattern could belong to an item being copied at that moment; that one clipboard item might not be saved to history.
clipboard.before_cleaning: Avoid cleaning while copying large items.
clipboard.catalog_concern: Narrow file patterns only (pending*.tmp, inProgress*.tmp), not the whole Clipboard folder (which holds pinned items). Good.

complus_cache.what: %windir%\Registration holds the COM+ catalog (R0000000000xx.clb files), the database of registered COM+ applications.
complus_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
complus_cache.risk: Deleting it corrupts COM+: Windows logs COM+ catalog errors, and services and installers that use COM+ can fail; repair needs a catalog restore or rebuild.
complus_cache.catalog_concern: Not a cache at all; a system database. Correctly disabled; it should arguably be on the deleter's refuse list.

coretemp_logs.what: Not documented. The path (Realtech\OpenHardwareMonitor) does not match Core Temp (by ALCPU) at all; it looks like a mistaken path.
coretemp_logs.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
coretemp_logs.catalog_concern: Label and path refer to different products.

corsair_logs.what: Not documented by the vendor in detail. Log files written by Corsair iCUE.
corsair_logs.used_for: Used for troubleshooting and by Corsair support. iCUE writes new logs as it runs.
corsair_logs.risk: Lost diagnostics if you need to report an iCUE problem.
corsair_logs.before_cleaning: Close iCUE first; files in use will be skipped.

crystaldiskinfo_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. CrystalDiskInfo normally stores settings and its S.M.A.R.T. history next to its program; an %APPDATA% folder is not documented.
crystaldiskinfo_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
crystaldiskinfo_cache.risk: If present, loses drive health history graphs and settings.
crystaldiskinfo_cache.catalog_concern: Whole app folder; health history is user data.

defraggler_logs.what: Not documented by the vendor. A whole Defraggler settings folder (exclusions, schedules).
defraggler_logs.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
defraggler_logs.risk: Loses Defraggler settings and exclude lists.
defraggler_logs.catalog_concern: Whole app folder, not a cache.

disk_nuker_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. A whole Disk Pulse data folder (monitoring configuration and history).
disk_nuker_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
disk_nuker_cache.risk: Loses monitoring setup and change history.
disk_nuker_cache.catalog_concern: Whole app folder; label names a different product (Disk Ninja).

duplicate_cleaner_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. A whole Duplicate Cleaner data folder (settings, saved scans).
duplicate_cleaner_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
duplicate_cleaner_cache.risk: Loses settings and saved scan results.
duplicate_cleaner_cache.catalog_concern: Whole app folder, not a cache.

easeus_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. A whole EaseUS data folder, which can include backup plan definitions and history.
easeus_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
easeus_cache.risk: Backup plans and history could disappear from the app.
easeus_cache.catalog_concern: Backup configuration, not cache; correctly disabled.

electron_updater_leftovers.what: Update installers downloaded by electron-updater (used by many Electron apps) into %LOCALAPPDATA%\<app>-updater\pending, plus a copied installer.exe.
electron_updater_leftovers.used_for: electron-updater installs a downloaded update when the app quits (autoInstallOnAppQuit). After deletion the app simply downloads the update again.
electron_updater_leftovers.risk: An update that is downloaded and waiting to install on quit is lost and re-downloaded; deleting during installation could interrupt it.
electron_updater_leftovers.before_cleaning: Close the app; do not clean while it is updating.
electron_updater_leftovers.catalog_concern: Listed safe; caution for the pending-install case. Folder is a real download cache, so re-download is the only cost.

em_client_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor for these subfolders. eM Client's log files and a temp folder inside its data folder (%APPDATA%\eM Client), which otherwise holds the mail database.
em_client_cache.used_for: Logs are for troubleshooting; temp holds files staged while opening or sending attachments. Both are recreated as needed.
em_client_cache.risk: An attachment you opened and edited from eM Client may live in temp until saved; deleting it loses those edits. Lost diagnostics.
em_client_cache.catalog_concern: Listed 'safe'; caution is better because temp can hold attachments being edited. Never widen the path: the parent folder is the mail database.

evernote_cache.what: Evernote's activity logs (%APPDATA%\Evernote\logs) and its Chromium/Electron HTTP cache folder.
evernote_cache.used_for: Logs record sync operations and errors for support; the cache speeds loading. Both are recreated. Notes (and unsynced changes) are stored elsewhere in the Evernote folder and are not targeted.
evernote_cache.risk: Lost diagnostics; logs can contain note titles, so deleting them is also a privacy plus. Never widen to %APPDATA%\Evernote: Evernote says unsynced notes live there.

evernote_full_cache.what: Same logs and cache as evernote_cache, plus a Thumbnails folder of note preview images.
evernote_full_cache.used_for: Thumbnails are regenerated from the notes. Note databases are NOT targeted, despite the label.
evernote_full_cache.risk: Same as evernote_cache; thumbnails redraw slowly at first.
evernote_full_cache.catalog_concern: Duplicates evernote_cache (same two paths). Label claims 'databases' but none are targeted, which is correct; fix the label so nobody adds them.

fax_account_cache.what: Not documented by Microsoft. Windows Fax and Scan keeps faxes and cover pages under ProgramData\Microsoft\Windows NT\MSFax and Documents\Fax; this path is not a documented cache.
fax_account_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
fax_account_cache.risk: Could hold received faxes or personal cover pages.
fax_account_cache.catalog_concern: Label says 'received fax staging' = user data.

filezilla_cache.what: FileZilla's settings folder: sitemanager.xml (saved servers, often with stored passwords), recentservers.xml, filezilla.xml and the transfer queue.
filezilla_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
filezilla_cache.risk: Deletes all saved FTP/SFTP sites and their credentials and settings.
filezilla_cache.catalog_concern: The label itself names sitemanager.xml; this is a credential store. Correctly disabled.

glary_utilities_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Glary Utilities keeps undo backups (registry backups made before repairs) in its data folder.
glary_utilities_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
glary_utilities_cache.risk: Loses the ability to undo registry repairs Glary made.

hdtune_logs.what: Not documented by the vendor. A whole HD Tune data folder (settings, saved results).
hdtune_logs.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
hdtune_logs.risk: Loses settings and saved benchmark/health results.

hwinfo64_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. HWiNFO keeps settings in HWiNFO64.INI next to its program; an %APPDATA% folder is not documented.
hwinfo64_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
hwinfo64_cache.risk: If present, loses sensor layouts and logging settings.

logseq_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. The Electron HTTP cache and log files of the Logseq desktop app (%APPDATA%\Logseq).
logseq_cache.used_for: Cache speeds loading; logs are for troubleshooting. Recreated automatically. Your graph (the markdown files and ~/.logseq) is elsewhere and not touched.
logseq_cache.catalog_concern: Label says 'graph database' but no graph data is targeted (good); fix the label.

m365_app_webview_cache.what: The Chromium Cache and Code Cache of the WebView2 browser inside the Microsoft 365 (Office) app package.
m365_app_webview_cache.used_for: Speeds loading of the app's web pages; rebuilt automatically.
m365_app_webview_cache.risk: None known; Local Storage/IndexedDB/cookies in the same EBWebView folder are not targeted.

macrium_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor for this path. Log files of Macrium Reflect in the user's profile.
macrium_cache.used_for: Logs describe past backup/restore runs. Deleting them does not affect image files or backup definitions.
macrium_cache.risk: Lost history of past backup jobs (what ran, what failed). Differential-chain metadata is in the image files, not here.
macrium_cache.before_cleaning: Close Macrium Reflect; no backup running.
macrium_cache.catalog_concern: Label says 'differential chain metadata' but only Logs is targeted; Macrium's main logs are under ProgramData, so this may find little.

macrium_reflect_logs.what: Not documented by the vendor. The whole %APPDATA%\Macrium folder (settings, backup definitions/XML, logs).
macrium_reflect_logs.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
macrium_reflect_logs.risk: Could remove saved backup definitions and schedules.
macrium_reflect_logs.catalog_concern: Whole app folder; macrium_cache already covers the Logs subfolder safely.

mendeley_cache.what: Mendeley Desktop's data folder: its local library database (references, annotations, highlights).
mendeley_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
mendeley_cache.risk: Loses unsynced references and PDF annotations; forces a full re-sync.

minitool_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. A whole MiniTool data folder (settings, saved recovery scan results).
minitool_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
minitool_cache.risk: Could lose a saved data-recovery scan you still need.

msi_afterburner_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Afterburner keeps profiles in its program folder; this %APPDATA% folder is not a documented cache.
msi_afterburner_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
msi_afterburner_cache.risk: If present, could hold overclock/fan profiles or monitoring logs.

notezilla_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. A cache and a logs subfolder inside Notezilla's data folder.
notezilla_cache.used_for: Presumably rebuilt by the app; logs are for troubleshooting.
notezilla_cache.risk: Unverified: if Notezilla keeps anything other than cache in 'cache', notes could be affected. Notes themselves are in its database files elsewhere.
notezilla_cache.catalog_concern: Listed safe with no vendor documentation for what 'cache' holds in a notes app; caution until verified on a real install.

notion_cache.what: Notion desktop is Electron: %APPDATA%\Notion holds Local Storage, IndexedDB, cookies (sign-in) and an offline copy of pages; %LOCALAPPDATA%\Notion holds app/updater files.
notion_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
notion_cache.risk: Signs you out and drops offline pages and unsynced edits.
notion_cache.catalog_concern: Label itself names IndexedDB; correctly disabled. A narrower entry could target %APPDATA%\Notion\Cache, Code Cache and GPUCache only.

nzxt_cam_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Whole NZXT CAM data folder (profiles, settings, possibly sign-in).
nzxt_cam_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
nzxt_cam_cache.risk: Loses RGB/fan profiles and may sign you out of CAM.

obsidian_cache.what: The Chromium HTTP cache ('Cache') and logs of the Obsidian desktop app in %APPDATA%\obsidian. The same folder also holds obsidian.json (your vault list), IndexedDB and Local Storage, which are not targeted.
obsidian_cache.used_for: Cache speeds loading of the app's resources and is rebuilt. Vault notes and plugins live inside each vault, not here.
obsidian_cache.risk: None known for Cache/logs. Never widen to the parent: deleting obsidian.json makes Obsidian forget your vaults; IndexedDB holds the metadata cache and sync state.
obsidian_cache.catalog_concern: Label mentions 'plugins' and 'vault cache' but neither is targeted (good); fix the label.

office_cache_extended.what: Cache, blob_storage and GPUCache of classic Microsoft Teams (%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Teams), an Electron app.
office_cache_extended.used_for: Microsoft's own fix for Teams problems is to delete everything in this folder; Teams rebuilds it, and the next start is slower. Classic Teams is retired; new Teams uses Packages\MSTeams_8wekyb3d8bbwe.
office_cache_extended.risk: None known for these three subfolders; first start is slower.
office_cache_extended.before_cleaning: Quit Teams (including the tray icon) first.
office_cache_extended.catalog_concern: Label promises OneNote, Publisher and Visio caches but only classic Teams paths are listed. New Teams is not covered.

office_clicktorun_cache.what: Not documented by Microsoft as a user-cleanable cache. Click-to-Run folders hold Office's update and setup pipeline state.
office_clicktorun_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
office_clicktorun_cache.risk: Can break or stall Office updates and repairs.
office_clicktorun_cache.catalog_concern: Servicing state for Office; correctly disabled.

office_temp.what: Not documented by Microsoft. Matches Excel*.tmp and Word*.tmp files in %TEMP% left behind by Office.
office_temp.used_for: Office creates temporary files while editing and saving; leftovers after a crash are not reused. AutoRecover files live elsewhere (%APPDATA%\Microsoft\Word/Excel) and are not targeted.
office_temp.risk: A matching file could belong to a document open right now; locked files are skipped by the deleter.
office_temp.catalog_concern: Label promises 'unsaved files and OfficeFileCache' but neither is targeted; good, those are user data and Office's upload cache. Fix the label.

outlook_new_webview_cache.what: The Chromium Cache, Code Cache and GPUCache of the WebView2 browser that new Outlook (olk.exe) uses to show its interface.
outlook_new_webview_cache.used_for: Speeds loading of Outlook's web interface; rebuilt on the next start. Mail is in Exchange/Outlook.com, not here.
outlook_new_webview_cache.risk: None known for these three folders. Deleting the whole EBWebView folder (not done here) would also clear add-in data and sign-ins.
outlook_new_webview_cache.catalog_concern: Correctly scoped to Cache/Code Cache/GPUCache, not EBWebView as a whole.

outlook_temp_cache.what: Classic Outlook's data folders: %LOCALAPPDATA%\Microsoft\Outlook holds .ost/.pst mail files; %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Outlook holds signatures-related settings, nicknames and rules exports.
outlook_temp_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
outlook_temp_cache.risk: Deletes mail stores (.pst = possibly the only copy of mail) and offline caches; Outlook must re-download everything or mail is lost.
outlook_temp_cache.catalog_concern: Consistent with the CLAUDE.md rule: .pst/.ost and Outlook data folders are always refused.

papers_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. The Papers (ReadCube) library folder: PDF library index, annotations, sync state.
papers_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.

paragon_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Whole Paragon data folder: backup catalog and job settings.
paragon_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
paragon_cache.risk: Backup jobs/catalog could be lost, making restores harder.

peazip_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. PeaZip's settings folder (configuration, bookmarks); extraction temp normally goes to %TEMP%.
peazip_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.

privacy_guardian_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Whole data folder of a 'Privacy Guardian' app.
privacy_guardian_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.

putty_cache.what: PuTTY stores sessions and SSH host keys in the registry (HKCU\Software\SimonTatham\PuTTY), not in this folder; its random seed file PUTTY.RND lives in Application Data.
putty_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
putty_cache.risk: Nothing cache-like to gain; the label's 'host keys and sessions' would be configuration if they were here.
putty_cache.catalog_concern: Label is wrong about where PuTTY keeps sessions; keep disabled.

quickbooks_cache.what: Not documented by Intuit as a cache. %APPDATA%\Intuit holds QuickBooks and other Intuit app data (license/entitlement and settings).
quickbooks_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
quickbooks_cache.risk: Can break QuickBooks licensing/registration and settings; label even names the audit trail.

readcube_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. ReadCube data folder with library cache and annotations.
readcube_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.

rufus_logs.what: Since Rufus 3.15, %LOCALAPPDATA%\Rufus holds the files Rufus downloads on demand (extra GRUB/Syslinux versions) and a log saved on exit.
rufus_logs.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. It could be re-enabled with a narrower path.
rufus_logs.risk: Rufus re-downloads those files when needed and falls back to its built-in copies offline. Settings are not stored here by default.
rufus_logs.catalog_concern: Disabling was over-cautious: per Rufus's own notes this folder is downloads + log. Could be re-enabled as safe.

simplenote_cache.what: Simplenote desktop (Electron) data folder: local notes database and sign-in state.
simplenote_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
simplenote_cache.risk: Signs you out and loses unsynced notes.

sparkle_logs.what: Not documented by any vendor. Sparkle is a macOS update framework; a %APPDATA%\sparkle\logs folder is not a known Windows location.
sparkle_logs.used_for: If it exists, presumably update-check logs.
sparkle_logs.catalog_concern: Likely matches nothing on Windows; harmless but dead.

ssh_keys_cache.what: known_hosts.old is the single backup copy OpenSSH's ssh-keygen writes when it edits known_hosts (ssh-keygen -R or -H).
ssh_keys_cache.used_for: Only useful to undo the last ssh-keygen edit. Nothing reads it automatically.
ssh_keys_cache.risk: You lose the ability to restore a host entry you just removed. It may contain unhashed host names, so deleting it is a privacy plus.
ssh_keys_cache.catalog_concern: Path is exactly the .old file; private keys, known_hosts and authorized_keys are not touched. Good.

sticky_notes.what: %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Sticky Notes is the LEGACY Sticky Notes folder; it holds StickyNotes.snt, the notes file of Windows 7/8 and early Windows 10. The entry targets only StickyNotes.sqm (usage data).
sticky_notes.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
sticky_notes.risk: The .sqm file itself is harmless; but the folder's .snt file may be the only copy of old notes not yet migrated to the new app.
sticky_notes.catalog_concern: The narrow .sqm pattern would be safe, but keeping the whole entry off avoids any risk to StickyNotes.snt.

stremio_webview_cache.what: The Chromium Cache and Code Cache of Stremio's WebView2 user data folder.
stremio_webview_cache.used_for: Speeds loading of Stremio's interface; rebuilt automatically. Sign-in lives in Local Storage/cookies, which are not targeted.

thrustmaster_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Thrustmaster T.A.R.G.E.T data folder: user scripts and controller profiles.
thrustmaster_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
thrustmaster_cache.risk: Loses custom joystick/HOTAS profiles and scripts.

thunderbird_cache.what: Thunderbird's network cache (cache2) and startup cache in each profile under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Thunderbird\Profiles. The mail, address books and settings live in the Roaming profile and are not targeted.
thunderbird_cache.used_for: cache2 holds downloaded remote content (images in messages, web pages); startupCache speeds start-up. Thunderbird recreates both.

veeam_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor for this path. Log files of a Veeam product in the user profile; Veeam Agent's main logs are under ProgramData.
veeam_cache.used_for: Logs are used for troubleshooting and by Veeam support; backups and catalogs are not here.
veeam_cache.risk: Lost diagnostics for failed backup jobs.
veeam_cache.catalog_concern: Label says 'metadata cache and catalog' but only Logs is targeted; fine, and probably finds little.

ventoy_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. Ventoy is mostly portable and keeps its plugin config (ventoy.json) on the USB drive; this local folder's purpose is undocumented.
ventoy_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.

voice_recorder_cache.what: LocalState of the Windows Voice Recorder / Sound Recorder app: app settings and state, possibly recordings depending on version.
voice_recorder_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
voice_recorder_cache.risk: Could delete recordings and app settings.

vscode_crashpad.what: Crash reports (minidumps) collected by Crashpad, the crash reporter built into VS Code (Electron).
vscode_crashpad.used_for: Pending reports wait to be uploaded or are kept for local analysis; nothing else needs them. New ones appear only after a crash.
vscode_crashpad.risk: Crashpad keeps PENDING reports until they upload; deleting them loses reports that may never have reached Microsoft, and you cannot attach a recent crash dump to a bug report.
vscode_crashpad.before_cleaning: Only after you no longer need to report a recent VS Code crash; close VS Code.

wifi_profiles_cache.what: Saved Wi-Fi profiles are kept by Windows in C:\ProgramData\Microsoft\Wlansvc\Profiles\Interfaces (XML per network). %APPDATA%\Microsoft\Windows\WLAN is not that location.
wifi_profiles_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
wifi_profiles_cache.risk: If it did target the real profiles, every saved Wi-Fi network and password would be forgotten.
wifi_profiles_cache.catalog_concern: Path is wrong and the intent (deleting saved Wi-Fi) is never a cleanup; keep disabled. Use 'netsh wlan delete profile' for that.

windows_camera_cache.what: LocalState of the Windows Camera app: settings and app state. Photos and videos are saved to Pictures\Camera Roll, not here.
windows_camera_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
windows_camera_cache.risk: Resets camera app settings; little space to gain.

windows_photo_viewer_cache.what: Not documented by Microsoft. Classic Windows Photo Viewer has no documented cache folder here; thumbnails are in Explorer's thumbcache.
windows_photo_viewer_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.

windows_photos_cache.what: LocalCache of the Microsoft Photos app package. Not documented in detail by Microsoft; packaged apps may keep WebView2 or sign-in data here (WhatsApp keeps its login under LocalCache).
windows_photos_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
windows_photos_cache.risk: Possible sign-out of OneDrive/Microsoft account in Photos, or loss of its index; would rebuild slowly.
windows_photos_cache.catalog_concern: Consistent with the 2026-10-11 WhatsApp incident: a whole LocalCache is not proof of a cache. Only specific cache subfolders should be offered.

winrar_cache.what: %APPDATA%\WinRAR is one of the two places WinRAR reads its license file rarreg.key from; it can also hold settings/themes.
winrar_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
winrar_cache.risk: Deleting it can un-register a paid WinRAR licence.

winscp_cache.what: A temp and a Logs folder under %APPDATA%\WinSCP. By default WinSCP puts temporary copies of remote files in the system %TEMP%, so these exist only if configured.
winscp_cache.used_for: Temp holds local copies of remote files opened for editing; WinSCP uploads changes from there. Logs are session logs.
winscp_cache.risk: A remote file open in an editor whose changes have not been uploaded yet would be lost. Lost session logs.
winscp_cache.before_cleaning: Close WinSCP and any files opened from it.
winscp_cache.catalog_concern: Listed safe; temp can hold edits not yet uploaded, so caution.

winzip_cache.what: Not documented by the vendor. WinZip's data folder (settings, history and possibly licence/registration data).
winzip_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.

wise_cache360_cache.what: The path is Wise Folder Hider's data folder, not Wise Care 365's. Wise Folder Hider hides and encrypts files and folders.
wise_cache360_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
wise_cache360_cache.risk: Users report hidden data can become inaccessible if the program's state is lost; deleting its data could cut you off from hidden files.
wise_cache360_cache.catalog_concern: Label names a different product; the folder belongs to a file-hiding tool. Keep disabled.

zotero_cache.what: %APPDATA%\Zotero is Zotero's profile folder (settings, and on old versions the library itself); the library (zotero.sqlite + storage\ PDFs) is normally in C:\Users\<you>\Zotero.
zotero_cache.used_for: Disabled in the catalog, so the app never cleans it. Keeping it disabled is correct.
zotero_cache.risk: Loses Zotero settings and, on older installs, the entire library and attachments.
zotero_cache.catalog_concern: Whole profile folder; old installs keep zotero.sqlite inside it.

squirrel_installer_temp.what: %LOCALAPPDATA%\SquirrelTemp: the working folder of Squirrel.Windows Setup.exe installers (used by many Electron apps). Vendors such as UiPath document SquirrelSetup.log there as the setup log.
squirrel_installer_temp.used_for: Installing or updating apps such as Discord or Slack. Nothing reads it after the install has finished.
squirrel_installer_temp.risk: SquirrelSetup.log, which explains a failed install, is lost. Installed apps are under their own folders and are not touched.
squirrel_installer_temp.before_cleaning: Do not clean while an app installer is running; files younger than a day are kept for that reason.

vscode_electron_cache.what: VS Code's Chromium/Electron 'Code Cache' (V8 compiled JavaScript) and 'GPUCache' (compiled GPU shaders).
vscode_electron_cache.used_for: Speeds up start-up and rendering; VS Code rebuilds both on the next start. Settings, extensions and workspace state are elsewhere and not targeted.
vscode_electron_cache.risk: Slightly slower first start after cleaning.
vscode_electron_cache.before_cleaning: Close VS Code (files in use are skipped).
